documents.title: Conference Call with the Fund Managers, Analysts and Investors - Transcript
Presentation - Conference Call with the Fund Managers, Analysts and Investors on October 29, 2026

analysis.summary: Wheels India Limited reported financial and operational results for Q2 FY27, highlighting growth in overall sales and export revenues. Management outlined expectations for full-year capex and detailed strategic focus areas spanning various automotive and industrial segments, including aluminum wheels, wind energy components, and hydraulic cylinders. The company also reported metrics regarding debt, working capital, and return ratios. Wheels India Limited presented its Q1 FY27 investor presentation, reporting consolidated gross revenues of Rs 1,492.79 crore, reflecting a 17.7% growth compared to Q1 FY26. Management outlined an estimated capital expenditure of Rs 400 to Rs 450 crore for FY27, planned to be funded predominantly through internal accruals while keeping debt at current levels.

guidance.claim: Capex for FY27 is estimated to be between Rs 400 crs and Rs 450 crs.
guidance.quote: Capex of FY27 is estimated to be in the region of Rs 400 to Rs 450 crs

demand_outlook.claim: The company strategy includes growing exports of wheels for construction equipment and agricultural tractors.
demand_outlook.quote: Grow exports of wheels for construction equipment and agricultural tractors

capex_expansion.claim: The planned capex is directed towards capacity expansion in auto steel wheels, cast alloy wheels, energy products division including large machining, hydraulic cylinders, construction & mining wheels, and air suspension.
capex_expansion.quote: This capex is towards expansion of capacity in auto steel wheels, cast alloy wheels, energy products division including large machining, hydraulic cylinders, construction & mining wheels and air suspension .

capex_expansion.claim: Capital expenditure for FY27 is projected to be in the range of Rs 400 to Rs 450 crore.
capex_expansion.quote: Capex of FY27 is estimated to be in the region of Rs 400 to Rs 450 crs

capex_expansion.claim: The company spent INR 261 crores towards capex in the previous year.
capex_expansion.quote: In terms of capex, last year, we basically spent about INR261 crores towards capex, which is both in terms of investment towards the windmill business, aluminium business and a little bit of the off-road businesses and some routine capex and cost savings totalling INR261 crores.

capex_expansion.claim: Management expects capex to be between INR 280 crores and INR 300 crores in the current year.
capex_expansion.quote: And we expect in the current year, it will be between INR280 crores to INR300 crores of capex.

capex_expansion.claim: The board-approved capex for financial year 2026-27 is about INR 280 crores.
capex_expansion.quote: One is the capex approved for the Board is about INR280 crores at the moment.

capex_expansion.claim: The company's aluminium wheel capacity is currently about 42,000 per month and is being increased to 60,000 in a few months, and then to 80,000 by half year.
capex_expansion.quote: In aluminium wheels we currently have a capacity of about 42,000 per month. We are increasing it -- in a few months we are increasing it to 60,000 and then by half year, we'll increase it to 80,000.

margins_costs.claim: Cost optimization remains a focus with a thrust on profitability.
margins_costs.quote: Cost optimization, with a thrust on profitability

margins_costs.claim: The company recorded a net forex profit of about INR 4 crores in the current quarter and close to INR 10 crores for the whole year.
margins_costs.quote: So in the current quarter, we had a profit of about INR4 crores as a net thing on the forex. And for the whole year, it is about close to INR10 crores as forex gain.

margins_costs.claim: The company introduced a phased inventory provisioning policy in the third quarter of FY26.
margins_costs.quote: So this is a policy that we kind of introduced in the third quarter of FY '26. And that is kind of what is reflecting in this.

orders_capacity.claim: Combined passenger car steel wheel capacity between Wheels India and its subsidiary is approximately 11 million to 12 million.
orders_capacity.quote: So if you take passenger car, steel wheels between us and our subsidiary, if I look at it combined, I think Wheels India has got a capacity of about 4 million and the subsidiary has got a capacity of about 7 million. So about 11 million to 12 million is the capacity.

capital_allocation.claim: Management intends to fund capex predominantly through accruals and hold debt at current levels.
capital_allocation.quote: Fund capex predominantly thro accruals and holding the debt at current levels

capital_allocation.claim: Management is targeting working capital optimization and cash flow management.
capital_allocation.quote: Working capital optimization and cash flow management

risks_headwinds.claim: Management noted that industrial fuel costs rose far ahead of general citizen prices, creating cost and availability issues.
risks_headwinds.quote: Industrial fuel costs went up far ahead of what has happened for the citizens of the country. So we had increases even as far back as March last year. So we had a fuel cost increase. Fuel availability was an issue.

management_commitments.claim: Capex for FY27 is estimated to be in the region of Rs 400 to Rs 450 crs.
management_commitments.quote: Capex of FY27 is estimated to be in the region of Rs 400 to Rs 450 crs

management_commitments.claim: The company plans to fund capital expenditure predominantly through accruals and keep debt at current levels.
management_commitments.quote: Fund capex predominantly thro accruals and holding the debt at current levels

management_commitments.claim: Management plans to ramp up the cast aluminium wheel business.
Management expects the company to be 1 or 2 years away from achieving double-digit EBITDA.
management_commitments.quote: So I think as and when that happens, I think we're probably 2 years away -- 1 or 2 years away from double-digit EBITDA.

_meta.note: Facts are verbatim-grounded against the company's own documents; claims whose quote was not found were dropped.
